text.p: Italy's BTP futures slipped lower due to caution on other bonds market, profit-taking and some concern over the dollar ticking up against the mark.

Dealers said the BTP market got off to a cautious start with the French audit of public finances due to be released today by the new socialist-led government, and Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony starting in the U.S. on Tuesday.
The weekend debate over Italy's 1998 budget had little effect with Treasury minister Ciampi finally confirming that the financial measure would be for 25 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures.
Dealers addded that the BTP market is now awaiting the publication of preliminary data on Italian July CPI from five ciites followed by a further six cites on Tuesday.
Analysts expected a flat month-on-month July CPI rate and an annual rate of 1.6 percent in July from a year-on-year rate of 1.4 percent in June.

Weekend papers reported that extra spending on education, early retirement pensions and other items might push the 1998 budget up to 28 trillion lire, but the Treasury minister Ciampi later confirmed the budget would remain at 25 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures.
Dealers added that bond markets were likely to be a little cautious ahead of the Humphrey Hawkins testimony to Congress by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan which starts on Tuesday.
